description: Adds one rule to a security group and returns it as the platform made it (with its id). Machines with the group get it at once. Adding a rule that already exists changes nothing and returns the existing one. Zero trust: open only the ports a service needs, from the narrowest source that works: another security group (remote_group_id) for your own machines, an address range for people or partners, 0.0.0.0/0 only for a public website's 80/443. When a machine gets a public URL, the platform opens that port to any address in every security group the machine has at that moment, and closes it when the URL is removed. A group attached later does not have it.

cidr.description: Inbound: who may connect. Outbound: where to. An address range such as 203.0.113.0/24, or one address. 0.0.0.0/0 is the whole internet (::/0 for IPv6): only for a public service. Give cidr OR remote_group_id; an inbound rule needs one.

description.description: Optional note shown with the rule, e.g. 'postgres from the app'.

direction.description: ingress (the default) = connections coming IN to machines in the group; egress = connections they make OUT. A new group already allows every outbound connection.

port.description: One port, e.g. 443. With tcp or udp. Use port_range_min and port_range_max for a range instead.

port_range_max.description: Last port of a range (with port_range_min).

port_range_min.description: First port of a range (with port_range_max).

protocol.description: tcp (the default), udp, icmp (ping), or any.

remote_group_id.description: Instead of cidr: only the machines in this other security group (e.g. a database group accepts 5432 only from the app group). The zero-trust way to connect your own machines.

security_group_id.description: The group the rule goes in: an id from list_security_groups (or create_security_group).

name: add_security_group_rule
title: Add security group rule
